Now I have a clear picture. The issue is in `src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py`. At line 2227, when `padding=True`, the code unconditionally warns that `max_length` is ignored. But this warning is incorrect when `truncation=True` is also set, because `max_length` IS used for truncation. The warning should only be raised when `max_length` is truly not going to be used (i.e., when truncation is not also active).

The fix is clear. The warning at line 2226 should only be raised when `max_length` is truly ignored — which is only the case when truncation is not also requested. When `truncation=True`, `max_length` is used for truncation even if `padding=True`.

The file that needs modification is:

- **`src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py`** — change line 2225-2226 from `if max_length is not None:` to `if max_length is not None and truncation is False:` (or equivalently `if max_length is not None and not truncation:`), so the warning is not raised when truncation is also active.

The issue is clear. The warning at line 2226-2227 in `src/transformers/tokenization_utils_base.py` is overly broad — it warns that `max_length` is ignored when `padding=True`, but `max_length` is still used for truncation when `truncation=True` is also set. The condition needs to be refined so the warning only fires when `max_length` is truly unused (i.e., truncation is not active).

The fix: Change the condition on line 2225 from `if max_length is not None:` to `if max_length is not None and truncation is False:`.
